record.paper_title: The Hamiltonian Seifert Conjecture: Examples and Open Problems
record.context_brief: Finite capacity of the standard symplectic torus
record.original_question: For the standard symplectic torus T^{2n} with n > 1, is the Hofer–Zehnder capacity finite? Equivalently, does the standard symplectic structure on T^{2n} give a compact symplectic manifold of finite Hofer–Zehnder capacity, even though the paper notes only partial almost-existence results under extra assumptions on the Hamiltonian?

evidence.quote: It seems to be unknown whether or not T2n with the standard symplectic structure has finite capacity for n > 1. However, almost existence has been proven for H : T2n → R satisfying some additional conditions; see, e.g., [Ji].

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $n \geq 2$ and consider the $2n$-dimensional torus $T^{2n} = \mathbb{R}^{2n}/\mathbb{Z}^{2n}$ equipped with the standard symplectic form $\omega_0 = \sum_{i=1}^{n} dx_i \wedge dy_i$ descended from the standard form on $\mathbb{R}^{2n}$. Recall that the Hofer–Zehnder capacity of a symplectic manifold $(M,\omega)$ is defined as
$$ c_{HZ}(M,\omega) = \sup\{\max H - \min H : H \in \mathcal{H}_a(M,\omega)\}, $$
where $\mathcal{H}_a(M,\omega)$ is the set of smooth, compactly supported (away from the boundary, if any) Hamiltonians $H : M \to \mathbb{R}$ such that:
(i) $H$ is locally constant near its extrema and on a nonempty open set;
(ii) the only periodic orbits of the Hamiltonian vector field $X_H$ (defined by $\iota_{X_H}\omega = -dH$) with period at most $1$ are constant orbits.

Question: Is the Hofer–Zehnder capacity $c_{HZ}(T^{2n},\omega_0)$ finite?
artifact.status_search_result: The finiteness of the Hofer–Zehnder capacity of $(T^{2n},\omega_0)$ with the standard (rational) symplectic structure, for $n\ge 2$, appears to remain open. Usher (Trans. AMS 2012) showed that many closed symplectic manifolds have infinite Hofer–Zehnder capacity, but his main earlier known example involved tori with an irrational symplectic structure, and recent surveys still describe the value of $c_{HZ}$ as unknown in many cases including this one. No paper found resolves the standard symplectic torus case.

status_evidence.title: Many Closed Symplectic Manifolds Have Infinite Hofer–Zehnder Capacity (M. Usher)
status_evidence.snippet: The only previous explicit example in the literature was the torus T^{2n} (n>=2) with an irrational symplectic structure.
status_evidence.claim: Usher's results yield many examples of infinite Hofer–Zehnder capacity, but the standard (rational) symplectic torus is not among the explicitly resolved cases.

status_evidence.title: Hofer–Zehnder capacity of disc tangent bundles of projective spaces
status_evidence.snippet: The Hofer–Zehnder capacity is fairly hard to compute and unknown in many cases.
status_evidence.claim: Recent literature still describes the Hofer–Zehnder capacity as unknown in many natural cases.
